message.content: In Christian theology, Jesus Christ is regarded as the central figure—often seen as the fulfillment of prophetic tradition rather than just another prophet. However, many Christians also hold prophets such as Moses (who led Israel out of Egypt) and Isaiah (whose writings anticipate messianic hope) in high esteem. Thus, while Jesus is typically viewed as the most pivotal figure, other prophets are also considered highly significant within the broader biblical narrative.
